subject.title: fix(sessions): cap in-memory session history to prevent unbounded growth

question: Should the no-limit Gateway history HTTP/SSE path intentionally become a 500-message recent window, with clients required to use cursor pagination for older messages?
rationale: Source, tests, and live proof show the cap works, but neither correctness checks nor contributor proof can choose a new client-visible default for maintainers.

options.title: Approve the 500-message window
options.body: Accept the proposed recent-history boundary and document that no-limit HTTP/SSE snapshots are bounded while cursor pagination provides full retrieval.

options.title: Choose a different shared boundary
options.body: Revise the cap to a maintainer-selected constant or existing shared history-window policy, then rerun the same initialization, append, refresh, and pagination proof.

options.title: Preserve unbounded semantics
options.body: Do not merge this shape and instead redesign the endpoint so callers explicitly opt into a bounded window without changing existing no-limit behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve the 500-message window
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed recent-history boundary and document that no-limit HTTP/SSE snapshots are bounded while cursor pagination provides full retrieval.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history surface appears to originate in the session-management/dashboard API work associated with this contributor.
